title: Adding suffixes to the end of words
examples: Why is it happiness and not happyness?

explain.say: Imagine a friend carries your heavy bag for you. They were full of help, so they were... helpful! Look at the board: help is the root word, the part we start with.

draw.text: Adding suffixes to the end of words

explain.say: Now the end chunk lights up: ful. A chunk added at the end of a word is called a suffix. ful means full of, and it has only one l. Can you turn care and joy into new words?
Here is the opposite suffix on the board: less, which means without. Careless means without care. Hopeless means without hope. See how ful and less make a pair?
Careful with this one! Happy ends in y. When we add ness, the y turns into i. Look at the first chunk: happi. So we write happiness. The same thing happens in happily. Can you spot the change?

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: y changes to i before ness

explain.say: Superb! The board shows four suffix families. Look at the first one: ly tells you how something is done, like quickly. Challenge: how many words can you build from play? Played, playful, player, playing...

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What job does the suffix do?

faq.a: A suffix is a group of letters added to the end of a word to change its meaning or its job, like ful in helpful or ly in quickly.

faq.q: Why does ful have only one l?
faq.a: When full becomes a suffix it drops one l. So we write helpful, careful and beautiful, never helpfull.

faq.q: When does y change to i?
faq.a: If a word ends in a consonant and then y, change the y to i before most suffixes: happy becomes happiness, cry becomes cried. Keep the y before ing: crying.
asks: Why is it happiness and not happyness?

faq.q: Do I double the last letter before a suffix?
faq.a: For short words with one vowel and then one consonant, double the consonant before a suffix that starts with a vowel: run becomes running, hop becomes hopped.
asks: Why does running have two n letters?

faq.q: What is the difference between a prefix and a suffix?
faq.a: A prefix goes at the front of a word, like un in unkind. A suffix goes at the end, like ness in kindness.

facts: A suffix can change a word's job: kind is an adjective, kindness is a noun and kindly is an adverb.
The suffix ful always has one l, even though the word full has two.

quiz.say: Add ness to lazy. Which spelling is correct?
quiz.show: Add ness to lazy. Which spelling is correct?
quiz.why: Consonant plus y: change the y to i, then add ness.

wrong.1: The y changes to i before ness.
wrong.2: Do not drop the y; turn it into i.

quiz.say: What does less mean in fearless?
quiz.show: What does less mean in fearless?

wrong.0: full of is the suffix ful, as in fearful.
wrong.2: more is the suffix er, as in faster.
